Compose Multiplatform, one screen from state to pixels · check

Know Compose underneath already?

One question for each of the 7 puzzles in this module. A right answer marks that puzzle as passed, so you can jump ahead. A wrong one tells you which puzzle to start with. Nothing is sent anywhere: it's saved in this browser.

Puzzle 0: What @Composable really does

You write a plain function, showName, that calls Text, and you forget the @Composable on it. You build. What happens?

Not quite. The check happens at compile time: the hidden parameter is missing in the call, so the code never gets to run. Learn it in puzzle 0 →

Right. No @Composable, no Composer to hand on, no build.

Not quite. The plugin rewrites only functions marked @Composable; showName stays a plain function. Learn it in puzzle 0 →

Puzzle 1: The tree Compose remembers

Above Counter(), whose count is 3, the code calls ErrorBanner() only if showError is true. showError was false, becomes true, and the screen runs again. What's Counter's count now?

Not quite. ErrorBanner's group is new, inside the if's group; Counter's group and slots stay Counter's. Learn it in puzzle 1 →

Not quite. The if's group was there even while showError was false; Counter's group never moved a place. Learn it in puzzle 1 →

Right. The if keeps a group of its own, so nothing after it shifts.

Puzzle 2: Which row is which?

Rows for Ana, Ben and Cleo come from a plain for-loop, with no key(). You remember a note in Cleo's row. Then Ana is removed from the top. Where does the note show now?

Not quite. Ben's call is first now, so it gets the first group, Ana's old one, which had no note. Learn it in puzzle 2 →

Not quite. Without key(), remember follows the position: the second call gets the second group. Learn it in puzzle 2 →

Right. Order decides: Cleo's call takes the second group, and the third group goes.

Puzzle 3: Who read that state?

Header reads one snapshot state, title, and Counter reads another, count. A tap changes only title. What runs again at the next frame?

Not quite. Screen didn't read title, so Screen isn't marked; Header restarts on its own. Learn it in puzzle 3 →

Not quite. Marks follow reads: Counter never read title, so it isn't marked. Learn it in puzzle 3 →

Right. A write marks only its own readers.

Puzzle 4: What gets skipped

Screen runs again and calls Profile(User(name)), building a new User each run. User is a data class with one val, a String, in your own module. name hasn't changed. Does Profile run?

Right. A stable argument is compared with equals.

Not quite. Each child call compares its arguments first; equal arguments skip. Learn it in puzzle 4 →

Not quite. Comparing by instance is for unstable types; a data class of vals is stable and compared with equals. Learn it in puzzle 4 →

Puzzle 5: One frame, from tree to pixels

A Column gets at most 300 pixels of width. Its child, a Text, needs 400 pixels to fit its words on one line. What happens when the Text is measured?

Not quite. A child picks its size within the constraints; it can't choose more than the maximum. Learn it in puzzle 5 →

Right. Within the constraints, so it wraps.

Not quite. Each child is measured once per layout; the constraints come first. Learn it in puzzle 5 →

Puzzle 6: Four layers, one edge per platform

Your shared code calls Button inside a Column, and you build it for iOS. Which layer on that path has the most code written only for iOS?

Right. Compose UI holds the biggest iOS edge.

Not quite. The slot table is shared; the runtime's few native files are about threads and the frame clock. Learn it in puzzle 6 →

Not quite. material3's only Apple-specific files are about dates; Button is shared code. Learn it in puzzle 6 →
